size_rationale: Medium because it is a half-applied rename whose gold fix spans two files, with the cause one step away from the three endpoints in the prompt and the resulting error swallowed by their catch blocks.
prompt: POST /v1/auth/refresh-tokens, POST /v1/auth/reset-password and POST /v1/auth/verify-email all reject valid, unexpired tokens with 401. Login, register and all of the /v1/users endpoints work normally.

root_cause.detail: userService.getUserById was renamed to getUser (definition, internal callers, export and user.controller) but auth.service.js still calls userService.getUserById in refreshAuth, resetPassword and verifyEmail; the TypeError is swallowed by each catch block and returned as 401. The gold fix reverts the rename; completing it at the three auth.service.js call sites also passes the tests.

fail_to_pass: tests/integration/auth.test.js > Auth routes > POST /v1/auth/refresh-tokens > should return 200 and new auth tokens if refresh token is valid
tests/integration/auth.test.js > Auth routes > POST /v1/auth/reset-password > should return 204 and reset the password
tests/integration/auth.test.js > Auth routes > POST /v1/auth/verify-email > should return 204 and verify the email
oracle.cmd: npx jest tests/integration/auth.test.js -t 'should return 200 and new auth tokens if refresh token is valid|should return 204 and reset the password|should return 204 and verify the email'
